summary: Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent inference hangs and long tail latencies starting 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Symptoms appear as request timeouts or stalled streaming responses. Customer SDK shows repeated client retries which increase request rate.

Impact:
- Several production routes for Nimbus Health experienced perceived latency > 30s, many clients closed streams and retried.
- User-facing workflows (document summarization pipeline) experienced ~12% failure rate during peaks.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-west-2 on customer's Dedicated instance.
- API requests routed through hosted API gateway with rate limiting and soft quota signals enabled for dedicated customers.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (concurrency ~120).
2) When a subset of requests receive 429s or soft-quota HTTP headers, client SDK retries with exponential backoff but short initial backoff (100ms).
3) Observed behavior: SDK retries overlap with original traffic window causing repeated 429s and long queuing behind the serving runtime.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 429 responses returned from gateway and occasionally 503 from upstream serving-runtime when queue grows.
- Client logs show retry storm patterns (batches of identical requests retried every ~200-800ms).
- Token-level cost spikes correlate with retry windows.

Expected behavior:
- Soft-quota signals should throttle politely without inducing retry storms that cascade into higher end-to-end latency.

Relevant logs/traces/dashboards:
- Kibana traces: trace IDs provided by customer (see comments).
- Console dashboard: route "nimbus-prod/summarize" shows latency percentiles and rate-limit counters (dashboard link in comment).
- Gateway logs indicate 4xx rate-limit code returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 in several sequences.

Temporary workaround (customer applied):
- Customer reduced client SDK concurrency and increased initial backoff to 800ms which reduced perceived stalls.

Priority justification:
- Customer-facing degradation affecting critical summarization workflows; dedicated customer on active contract.

Requested action:
- Determine whether gateway soft-quota signals are being emitted too aggressively for dedicated customers during short bursts.
- Recommend mitigation: improved headers for retry guidance (Retry-After or explicit soft-quota TTL) and temporary tuning to backoff defaults in customer SDKs.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC — Support replicated pattern using customer's concurrency profile against staging gateway. Observed 4xx responses with no explanatory Retry-After header in several sequences.

2026-03-10 06:45 UTC — SRE throttling hypothesis: gateway layer is applying burst-window enforcement then falling back to per-account soft quota. Need to check token-bucket config for dedicated pools.

2026-03-10 09:20 UTC — Correlated spikes in request count with billing meter logs; meter shows transient spike in token consumption consistent with retries, not initial user requests. This implies amplification by client retries.
2026-03-11 11:05 UTC — Serving runtime queue depth rose to >500ms 95th percentile during retry windows; upstream returned 503 when autoscaler could not provision fast enough for sudden replays.

2026-03-11 14:00 UTC — Found missing Retry-After header on many 429 responses from the gateway when soft-quota policy triggered. Gateway code path for dedicated pools uses soft-quota signal without setting Retry-After for sub-second suppression.
2026-03-11 16:30 UTC — Customer reduced concurrency and adjusted SDK backoff; error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% during the same test bursts.
Next steps: add Retry-After to 429 soft-quota responses, evaluate increasing initial suppression window for dedicated pools (config change), and update SDK guidance for backoff defaults.
comments: 2026-03-10 00:40 UTC — Maria Chen (Support): Thanks for the report. Can you share a sample request ID and the SDK version? Also send a representative trace from Kibana so we can correlate gateway and runtime logs.
2026-03-10 01:05 UTC — Nimbus Health (Customer): Provided trace IDs: trace-9812, trace-9817. SDK v2.4.1. Added sample request JSON in attachment (see ticket attachments).

2026-03-10 06:55 UTC — Omar Patel (SRE): Replicated a similar burst against staging; seeing repeated 429s without Retry-After. Opening investigation with gateway team. Routing to component owners: @gateway-team, @serving-runtime.

2026-03-10 12:30 UTC — Gateway Engineer (internal): Found that soft-quota enforcement for dedicated accounts is using fast-path QoS that emits a custom header X-Soft-Quota-Expires but not Retry-After. Will prototype adding Retry-After values and test rollback window.
2026-03-11 15:10 UTC — Nimbus Health (Customer): We tested reducing concurrency and increasing backoff — clear improvement. Happy to run another test once you have a gateway tweak.

2026-03-12 08:00 UTC — Omar Patel (SRE): Planned change: emit Retry-After=0.8s for soft-quota 429s for dedicated pools and increase burst suppression to 1s. Will schedule rollout to canary tomorrow. Keeping ticket open while we validate.
resolution: In progress — mitigation planned. Gateway will emit Retry-After for soft-quota 429s and adjust suppression window for dedicated pools. Customer advised to update SDK backoff defaults as a complementary measure. Post-deployment validation required.
